card.name: Inside dys-/hyper- lab condition terms
card.fires_on: The middle piece of long medical condition words that start with dys- or hyper-/hypo-, such as the "lip" in dyslipidemia or "nat" in hypernatremia. It is strongest right after the prefix, before the word ending.

modes.label: Dyslipidemia
modes.description: The "lip" piece after "dys" in the metabolic risk list of dyslipidemia.
modes.example: women with hypertension, dys<<lip>>idemia, diabetes, or obesity.

modes.label: Electrolyte terms
modes.description: The middle piece of hypernatremia or hypophosphatemia, where a blood-level word is split.
modes.example: Avoid in patients with or at risk for hyper<<nat>>remia.

card.writes: It seems to push toward the remaining pieces of the word being spelled out, and away from unrelated word starts.
card.plain: It fires in the middle of long words for abnormal blood levels, like dyslipidemia or hypernatremia.
